climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Gewürztraminer, Riesling and Sauvignon Blanc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Pinot Noir and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water. Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
Faces the morning sun. Early light dries the dew, which cuts disease, and the grapes are spared the hottest afternoon sun.
